metaDescription: The history of The MuSiK Box and In Audio We Trust, from its Cleveland beginnings to the final posts in 2012.

header.title: The Story of The MuSiK Box & In Audio We Trust
header.intro: From Cleveland high school hallways to a growing community of listeners: the oral history and digital chronicle of an era-defining music publication.

genesis.title: The High School Genesis & The 'MSK' Code
genesis.bannerCaption: The MuSiK Box turntable banner · original mark on white
genesis.intro: In late 2008 and early 2009, during their sophomore year at **Saint Ignatius High School** in Cleveland, Ohio, co-founders **Myles Snider** and **Seamus Kelleher** launched an underground music destination straight from their laptops: *The MuSiK Box* (`themusikbox.com`).
genesis.nameOrigin: The publication's distinct capitalization was a subtle in-joke and personal signature: **The MuSiK Box** cleverly embedded the co-founders' initials — **M**yles **S**nider and **S**eamus **K**elleher — spelling out **MSK** within *MuSiK* using lowercase "u" and "i".
genesis.platforms: Built on early WordPress architectures and powered by DatPiff mixtape rips, Mediafire downloads, and direct email submissions from hungry indie artists, the site stood at the vanguard of the burgeoning music-blog revolution.

grog.title: Mac Miller at The Grog Shop & The MGK Video
grog.intro: The MuSiK Box booked **Mac Miller**'s first out-of-town headlining show at **The Grog Shop** in Cleveland Heights, held on August 21, 2010. Seamus and Myles worked with Cleveland promotion crew *The Coventry Kids* to bring the 18-year-old Pittsburgh rapper to the venue. Mac later recalled the show in the interview below.
grog.arroyoTitle: Mac Miller cites The Grog Shop — House of Blues Cleveland, Oct 10, 2011
grog.arroyoQuote: “Cleveland, little fun fact for you: actually the first out-of-town headlining show I ever did was at the Grog Shop.”
grog.liveIntro: On August 21, 2010, an 18-year-old Mac Miller drove out from Pittsburgh to play his maiden out-of-town headlining concert at The Grog Shop in Cleveland Heights. Documenting that night is a 1-minute live clip uploaded directly to Mac's official verified YouTube channel (@macmiller) in 2010.
grog.liveContext: Today, across a channel with over 5.04 million subscribers and hundreds of videos spanning a global legacy, [Mac Miller Live at The Grog Shop](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5nHcZ6xBzJ8) stands as one of the single oldest surviving uploads on his entire account—an immutable historical record of his first show outside Pittsburgh.
grog.mgkIntro: Earlier that year, on **April 22, 2010**, the co-founders shot a now-legendary parking lot interview on an iPhone in the school lot with a 19-year-old **Machine Gun Kelly (MGK)**, breaking down his breakout mixtape *100 Words and Running*.
grog.mgkCaption: Shot on an iPhone in the Saint Ignatius High School parking lot on April 22, 2010 — four months before Mac Miller's Grog Shop headline — this interview captures a 19-year-old MGK breaking down *100 Words and Running* at the cusp of his Lace Up breakout.
grog.mgkWatch: Watch the full restored clip on YouTube: [Machine Gun Kelly — The MuSiK Box Parking Lot Interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WzgJwyb199w).

surge.title: The Viral Surge & The 100k Ceiling
surge.readership: Historical readership estimates recorded for this retrospective put *In Audio We Trust* at 2,000 to 6,000+ daily readers in 2011. On record-shattering days, viral algorithmic traffic from **StumbleUpon**, Reddit, Hype Machine, DJ Earworm mashups, and college network word-of-mouth propelled single-day visitor counts above **100,000 unique visitors**. These figures describe occasional peaks, not typical daily traffic; contemporary analytics are not included in this archive.
surge.mashups: A major engine of this explosive growth was the golden age of collegiate mashup culture. IAWT was a premiere launchpad for artists like **The White Panda**, The Hood Internet, Super Mashed Bros, Norwegian Recycling, Brenton Duvall, and Big Z Remixes.

rebrand.title: The 301 Rebrand to In Audio We Trust
rebrand.bannerCaption: IAWT 2.0 Jefferson coin emblem and needle wordmark
rebrand.intro: As readership expanded beyond Ohio into a national footprint, the co-founders orchestrated a comprehensive brand evolution in early 2011, executing a 301 permanent redirect from `themusikbox.com` to `inaudiowetrust.com`.
rebrand.design: "IAWT 2.0" introduced a sleek, high-contrast dark aesthetic, custom audio streaming players, categorized music channels, and the Thomas Jefferson in DJ headphones emblem that became the brand's signature seal.
rebrand.contributors: To keep up with the unrelenting volume of PR submissions and exclusive premieres, the blog's circle grew the way so many 2009–2012 college-era sites did — friends pitching in between classes, guest writers dropping album reviews, and late-night track tips landing in the inbox. Core contributors included **{{writers}}**, who helped review tracks, cover shows, and manage the daily premiere queue.
rebrand.attributionNote: …and other contributors we're surely forgetting. If you wrote for us, sent in music, or helped run the site during those years, please reach out so we can claim your byline and get your name properly added to the record.

finale.title: Early Artist Coverage & The Final Posts
finale.intro: What made The MuSiK Box & IAWT unique was their track record of identifying future megastars months or years before mainstream recognition — tracking early mixtapes of **Tyler, The Creator, A$AP Rocky, Macklemore, Skrillex, Avicii**, Kendrick Lamar, Childish Gambino, The Weeknd, Frank Ocean, and more.
finale.sale: By early 2012, Seamus and Myles were college freshmen living in different cities. The publication had grown into a beast that demanded multiple posts daily, relentless track scouring, and constant coordination. Realizing they could not maintain the high editorial standards and hands-on curation they had established from separate college campuses, they made the decision to sell the blog in early 2012—officially concluding their authentic founder run on **January 25, 2012**.
finale.memories: For 15 years, until the compilation of this archive was established, they thought only their memories — and the still-regular reminders of its impact from some former readers via DM — would be all they had to remember this fun time from.
